conventions.convention: The operator and reconstruction family are fixed. A noise-level-free rule is a deterministic function α:Y→(0,∞) whose input is the observed datum, without the exact datum or noise bound.
Worst-case convergence is required separately at every exact datum in D(K†), over the entire closed data-error ball, including the exact datum itself. It is not uniform convergence over exact data.
The pseudoinverse has domain R(K)⊕R(K)⊥, returns the minimum-norm preimage of the range component, and carries the domain norm inherited from Y. Countable Choice is assumed.
The counterexample uses positive coordinate labels j≥1, truncation at floor(1/α), an empty sum when that bound is zero, and α(0)=1.
Power source order ν means |K|^ν=(K*K)^(ν/2). The centered modulus constrains one source element x by ||Kx||≤δ.
The finite-grid L-curve uses λ as the coefficient of the squared Tikhonov penalty, assigns curvature only to middle retained indices, and breaks ties by smallest original index.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice, a compact Hilbert operator K with discontinuous K†, maps Rα:Y→X converging pointwise to K† on D(K†) as α↓0, and a deterministic noise-level-free rule α:Y→(0,∞). If E_y(δ):=sup{||R_{α(z)}z−K†y||:z∈Y, ||z−y||≤δ} tends to zero as δ↓0 for every y∈D(K†), then K† is continuous on D(K†). Thus no such rule gives the stated convergence when K† is discontinuous; restricted solution or error classes, stochastic noise models, and finite-dimensional problems are not excluded.

For a fixed compact Hilbert inverse model K:X→Y and fixed reconstruction maps Rα:Y→X, a deterministic parameter-choice rule is a function α:Y→(0,∞). It is noise-level-free when α(z) uses only K, the fixed family, and z, without the exact datum or noise bound δ as input. Its reconstruction is R_{α(z)}z.
